language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, my name is James. I am from Scotland. My father owns a kiltstore in a small village where I live. A kilt looks like a skirt, but this one is traditionally worn by men.
Today, I am gonna wear a kilt during a parade. I am really excited. But I have a small problem. I lost my watch so I can't see what time the parade starts.
Luckily I know that there is an alternative way to tell the time. By looking at shadows! Do you know how this works?
Hi, my name is Tim. I am a friend of James. If you need any extra information, click me and I will help you. Good luck!

Now I can see where the sun is by looking at shadows. How would this be related to time?
I like to know what time it is, can you help me? We've learned that the sun casts a shadow when it blocks light. The shadow depends on the location of the sun.
The sun travels across the sky the same way, each day. For example, in the morning the sun is in the east, at noon it's right above us, and the sun sets in the west.
So, by looking at the sun, we can calculate the time. It's even easier to guess the time when we look at shadows. Do you want to try this trick?
Look at the length and position of the shadow. If you know that the sun rises in the east and moves to the west, what time do you think it is in the picture?

helperSimple.text: Look at the shadow. Where do you think the sun is? Guess the time based on the location of the sun.
